profile.reading: This is a Credit Suisse data center at 201 Main Avenue in Clifton, Passaic County, New Jersey, listed in industry directories as a fully operational facility, though neither square footage nor power capacity in megawatts is publicly disclosed for this location, and no confirmed year built was found in sourcing checked this session. Credit Suisse was a major Swiss bank until it collapsed into a UBS acquisition, announced March 19, 2023 for about 3.25 billion dollars, finalized in June 2023 to prevent a wider financial crisis; Credit Suisse Schweiz ceased to exist as a separate legal entity by July 2024, and Credit Suisse as a corporate entity is reported to have ceased to exist entirely by May 31, 2024, as UBS completed its integration of the acquired banks operations. This registry found no source confirming this specific Clifton, New Jersey facilitys current branding or operational status following that integration, meaning it is not confirmed whether the site continues operating under Credit Suisse branding, has been rebranded under UBS, has been repurposed for other UBS infrastructure, or has been decommissioned; this registry records the facility under its historical Credit Suisse identity, consistent with the operator name on this record, while noting this post-acquisition status uncertainty honestly rather than asserting a current operational state it could not verify. Clifton and the wider Passaic and Bergen County area of northern New Jersey have long hosted back office and data processing operations for major New York City area financial institutions, a pattern shared with other bank operated facilities in nearby New Jersey counties tracked elsewhere in this registry, including Barclays and BNY Mellon sites.

reading.body:
Credit Suisse operates a data center in Clifton, Passaic County, New Jersey that the operator does not publish power capacity or square footage for. The facility appears to be a private corporate data center rather than a marketed colocation or cloud service, and no specification detail is available from the operator's public sources.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 megawatts. This Clifton facility ranks sixth in the state by published megawatts, which means it publishes no figure and therefore does not appear in the state's published capacity total.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI infrastructure. The operator's choice not to disclose power or space figures leaves its relevance to AI scaling unknown.
